title: incident.v1
description: The `incident.yaml` of an incident directory `incidents/<name>/`. A fault incident has the executables `inject` and `heal` beside it, and optionally `probe`. A load incident has no `inject` or `heal`: the runner starts and stops the profile stream its event names, and an optional `probe` may follow. It says what the incident does and to what; it never says what impact is tolerated. ADR-0049.

name.description: Equal to the directory name; unique on the search path. The `incident` label of `sip_chaos_event`.

kind.description: `fault`: its executables act on a deployed component. `load`: the runner starts a profile stream at inject and stops it at heal.

target.description: Fault only: the pods the incident acts on. A run profile event may override it.

pick.description: `one`: the executable picks one live pod of the selector (and names it on stdout). `all`: every pod of the selector.

stop.description: Load only. `drain`: at heal the stream stops placing calls, its calls finish, then its generator is removed. `abandon`: at heal the generator is killed with its calls in flight, which leaves them to the system under test; its calls write no record and the stream is left out of the reconciliation.

params.description: Fault only: the incident's parameters. A parameter without `default` must be set by the run profile event. A default the schema cannot type-check is checked by the runner.

duration_s.description: The default time between `injected` and `heal`. 0 heals at once (a kill whose recovery is the platform's own).

expected_s.description: The usual time from `inject` to `recovered`, used by the dry-run's overlap check. Default `duration_s` + 60.

probe_s.description: How long after `healed` the probe may keep answering not-yet before the event fails.

requires.description: Capabilities the incident needs from the lab (`kind`, `docker`, `chaos-mesh`, …). The runner refuses a profile whose lab lacks one, before the run starts.
